name: 3 Ply Mask
description: Disposable 3-Ply Face Mask — single-use protective face mask with a three-layer filtration system designed to block dust, allergens, pollen, and airborne particles. The outer hydrophobic non-woven layer repels fluid splashes, the middle melt-blown polypropylene filter layer captures fine particles, and the inner soft non-woven layer absorbs moisture for comfortable breathing. Elastic ear loops provide a secure yet gentle fit without causing ear fatigue during extended wear. Adjustable aluminium nose clip moulds to the bridge of the nose for a snug, gap-free seal that reduces fogging on eyeglasses. Lightweight and breathable — suitable for continuous wear during patient visits, clinic shifts, and daily activities.
how_to_use: Remove the mask from its packaging by handling the ear loops only — avoid touching the filter surface. Identify the coloured side as the outer layer and the white side as the inner layer (facing your mouth). Place the mask over your nose and mouth. Loop the elastic ear loops around each ear. Press the aluminium nose clip firmly over the bridge of your nose to create a snug seal. Adjust the bottom edge to cover the chin fully. Dispose of the mask after single use or if it becomes damp, soiled, or damaged. Do not reuse, wash, or share masks.
key_features: Three-layer filtration system (outer non-woven + melt-blown polypropylene filter + inner soft non-woven) | Adjustable aluminium nose clip for snug, gap-free seal | Elastic ear loops for comfortable, fatigue-free extended wear | Lightweight and breathable for all-day use | Fluid-repellent outer layer | Moisture-absorbent inner layer | Disposable for hygiene compliance | Reduces eyeglass fogging with proper nose clip adjustment
ideal_for: General infection prevention in healthcare settings | Hospital and clinic visits | Home healthcare and patient care | Dust and pollution protection during commuting | Housekeeping and cleaning activities | Allergy season protection | Post-surgical wound care environments | Daily protective wear in crowded spaces
faqs:
Q: How often should I replace a 3 Ply Mask? A: Replace after each use or when the mask becomes damp, soiled, or difficult to breathe through — typically every 4–8 hours of continuous wear.
Q: Can I wash and reuse a 3 Ply Mask? A: No, 3 Ply masks are designed for single use. Washing degrades the melt-blown filter layer and significantly reduces filtration efficiency.
Q: Does a 3 Ply Mask protect against COVID-19? A: A 3 Ply mask provides a physical barrier that helps reduce the spread of respiratory droplets. For higher-risk environments, consult your healthcare provider about N95 or equivalent respirators.

name: AMBU Bag
description: AMBU Bag (Silicone) — self-inflating manual resuscitator bag made from durable, medical-grade silicone for emergency positive-pressure ventilation. Designed to deliver controlled breaths to patients who are not breathing or breathing inadequately, this is an essential life-saving device for emergency rooms, ambulances, ICUs, and home ventilation backup kits. Medical-grade silicone construction is autoclavable at 134°C, enabling full sterilisation and reuse across multiple patients. Self-inflating mechanism re-expands automatically after each squeeze, eliminating the need for an oxygen source (though supplemental O₂ can be attached). Transparent face mask allows real-time monitoring of the patient's lip colour and any vomiting during resuscitation.
how_to_use: Attach the appropriately sized mask to the bag outlet valve. Tilt the patient's head back slightly to open the airway (head-tilt, chin-lift manoeuvre). Place the mask firmly over the patient's nose and mouth, creating an airtight seal using the C-E hand technique — thumb and index finger form a 'C' over the mask while the remaining fingers lift the jaw. Squeeze the bag with the other hand to deliver a breath over 1 second, watching for visible chest rise. Release the bag to allow passive exhalation. Deliver breaths at the appropriate rate: adults 10–12 breaths/min, children 12–20, infants 20–30. Connect supplemental oxygen if available. After use, disassemble and autoclave all silicone components.
key_features: Medical-grade silicone — autoclavable at 134°C for full sterilisation and reuse | Self-inflating mechanism operates without an external oxygen source | Transparent mask for real-time patient monitoring (lip colour, vomiting) | Compatible with supplemental oxygen reservoir attachment | Non-rebreathing patient valve prevents exhaled air re-entry | Available in adult, paediatric, and infant sizes | Durable construction for reliable emergency performance | Compact and portable for ambulance and emergency bag storage
ideal_for: Emergency resuscitation (cardiac arrest, respiratory failure) | Ambulance and pre-hospital emergency care | ICU and critical care manual ventilation | Operating room backup ventilation | Home ventilation emergency backup | Code blue response and crash cart equipment | Patient transport ventilation | Training and simulation for CPR and BLS courses
faqs:
Q: What sizes of AMBU Bag are available? A: AMBU bags typically come in Adult, Paediatric, and Infant sizes. Select the size that matches the patient's age and lung capacity for effective ventilation.
Q: How do I sterilise an AMBU Bag after use? A: Silicone AMBU bags can be autoclaved or cleaned with hospital-grade disinfectant. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the specific sterilization method and temperature limits.
Q: Can a single person operate an AMBU Bag effectively? A: While one-person operation is possible, two-person technique (one to hold the mask seal, one to squeeze the bag) is recommended for better tidal volume delivery and mask seal.
Q: How do I know if the AMBU Bag is delivering adequate ventilation? A: Watch for visible chest rise with each squeeze. If the chest does not rise, reposition the airway, check the mask seal, and ensure there is no obstruction.

name: Abduction Pillow
description: Tynor Abduction Pillow — anatomically contoured high-density foam pillow engineered to maintain correct hip abduction positioning after total hip replacement surgery, hip fracture fixation, or hip dislocation reduction. The wedge-shaped design keeps the legs properly separated at the physician-prescribed angle, preventing the operated hip from crossing the midline — a critical precaution against post-surgical dislocation. Adjustable hook-and-loop straps secure the pillow between the thighs during sleep and rest, eliminating the risk of the legs drifting together unconsciously. The pillow's tapered shape (narrower at the knees, wider at the thighs) mirrors the natural anatomy for comfortable positioning. Removable, machine-washable cover maintains hygiene throughout the recovery period.
how_to_use: Place the pillow between the legs with the wider end positioned between the upper thighs and the narrower end between the knees. The flat surfaces should rest against the inner thighs. Secure the adjustable straps around each thigh to hold the pillow firmly in place. Use while sleeping, resting in bed, or any time the legs may drift together. The pillow should be used continuously for the duration prescribed by your orthopaedic surgeon — typically 6–12 weeks post-surgery. Remove the washable cover periodically for cleaning. Hand wash or machine wash the cover on a gentle cycle; air dry.
key_features: Anatomically contoured wedge shape maintains prescribed hip abduction angle | High-density foam provides firm, consistent positioning without compressing flat | Adjustable hook-and-loop straps secure pillow during sleep | Tapered design (wider at thighs, narrower at knees) for natural comfort | Removable, machine-washable cover for hygiene | Tynor quality construction for reliable post-surgical support | Lightweight and portable for bed or recliner use | Radiolucent foam does not interfere with post-surgical imaging
ideal_for: Post total hip replacement surgery (THR) — dislocation prevention | Hip fracture internal fixation recovery | Hip dislocation reduction aftercare | Revision hip arthroplasty | Hip abduction maintenance during sleep and rest | Orthopaedic post-operative positioning | Rehabilitation facilities and transitional care | Home healthcare post-surgical recovery
faqs:
Q: What is an Abduction Pillow used for? A: An abduction pillow is used after hip replacement surgery to keep the legs separated at a prescribed angle, preventing dislocation of the new hip joint during the critical healing period.
Q: How long do I need to use an Abduction Pillow after surgery? A: Typically 6–12 weeks post-surgery, but follow your orthopaedic surgeon's specific instructions as the duration varies based on the surgical approach and individual recovery.
Q: Can I sleep on my side while using an Abduction Pillow? A: Only if your surgeon permits it. When side-sleeping is allowed, the pillow should remain between your knees to maintain the correct abduction angle.

name: Adjustable Bed Railing
description: ABS Bed Side Railing — durable ABS plastic bed safety rail designed to prevent patient falls from hospital beds, home care beds, and adjustable beds. Foldable design allows the rail to be lowered flat for easy patient entry and exit, then raised and locked upright during sleep or rest. Universal clamp mechanism fits securely onto most standard bed frames without tools. Smooth, rounded edges and gap-free design eliminate entrapment hazards. Lightweight ABS plastic construction is strong enough to withstand leaning pressure while remaining easy to install and reposition. The rail also serves as a grab bar, giving patients a sturdy handhold when getting in and out of bed.
how_to_use: Position the railing along the side of the bed where fall risk is highest (typically the patient's weaker or operated side). Attach the clamp mechanism under the mattress and around the bed frame — tighten firmly until the rail does not wobble when pushed. Raise the rail upright and confirm it locks in the fully extended position. To allow patient access, release the locking mechanism and fold the rail flat below mattress level. Always re-raise and lock the rail when the patient is in bed. Check clamp stability daily and retighten if needed. Wipe clean with disinfectant.
key_features: Durable ABS plastic — strong, lightweight, and easy to clean | Foldable design for easy patient bed entry and exit | Universal clamp fits most standard hospital and home bed frames | Tool-free installation and repositioning | Smooth, rounded edges eliminate entrapment hazards | Doubles as a grab bar for sit-to-stand assistance | Locking mechanism holds rail securely in raised position | Lightweight for easy transport between rooms
ideal_for: Fall prevention for elderly and disoriented patients | Post-surgery bed safety (hip, knee, spine) | Patients with mobility impairment or balance issues | Home healthcare beds and adjustable beds | Hospital and nursing home patient safety | Dementia and confusion-related fall risk | Nighttime fall prevention | Sit-to-stand transfer assistance
faqs:
Q: Will the bed railing fit my hospital bed? A: Most bed railings are designed to fit standard hospital bed frames. Check the rail's clamp or bracket specifications against your bed frame dimensions before purchase.
Q: Can the bed railing be folded down? A: Yes, most models feature a fold-down mechanism so the railing can be lowered when the patient needs to get in or out of bed, and raised during rest.
Q: Is the bed railing safe for confused or restless patients? A: Bed railings can help prevent falls, but should be used with caution for agitated patients. Ensure there are no gaps where limbs could become entrapped, and follow facility safety protocols.

name: Air Bed Mattress
description: Naulakha Alternating Pressure Air Mattress — electric pump-driven air mattress system designed to prevent and treat pressure ulcers (bedsores) in bedridden patients. The mattress features rows of alternating air cells that cyclically inflate and deflate on a timed cycle, continuously redistributing body weight so no single skin area bears sustained pressure. This alternating pressure action promotes blood circulation to vulnerable pressure points (sacrum, heels, shoulders) and significantly reduces the risk of tissue breakdown. Adjustable pressure dial allows caregivers to set firmness based on the patient's body weight for personalised comfort and therapeutic effectiveness. Medical-grade PVC construction is waterproof, easy to wipe clean, and resistant to punctures. Whisper-quiet pump operates without disturbing the patient's sleep.
how_to_use: Place the air mattress flat on top of the existing bed surface (can be used over a regular mattress or directly on a bed frame). Ensure the air cells run horizontally across the bed. Connect the pump tubing to the mattress inlet valve. Plug the pump into a power outlet and turn on. Adjust the pressure control dial to match the patient's weight — heavier patients require higher pressure, lighter patients lower pressure. The pump will automatically cycle the air cells in an alternating pattern. Check regularly that all cells are inflating properly and no cells remain flat. Place a bed sheet over the mattress for comfort. Clean the mattress surface with a damp cloth and mild disinfectant. Do not use sharp objects near the mattress.
key_features: Alternating pressure cell system for continuous pressure redistribution | Adjustable pressure dial for patient weight-based customisation | Whisper-quiet electric pump for undisturbed sleep | Medical-grade PVC — waterproof, puncture-resistant, easy to clean | Promotes blood circulation to vulnerable pressure points | Places over existing bed or bed frame | Naulakha brand quality and reliability | Lightweight pump unit with tubing for easy setup
ideal_for: Bedsore (pressure ulcer) prevention and treatment | Long-term bedridden patients at home or in hospital | Post-surgical immobility and extended bed rest | Elderly care and geriatric nursing | Spinal cord injury patients | Palliative and hospice care | ICU step-down and transitional care | Home healthcare for immobile patients
faqs:
Q: How does an Air Bed Mattress prevent bedsores? A: The alternating pressure system inflates and deflates individual air cells in a cyclical pattern, continuously shifting pressure points across the body so no single area bears sustained load — this promotes blood circulation and prevents tissue breakdown.
Q: How often should I check the air pressure? A: Check the pump and mattress daily. Ensure the pump is running, all cells are inflating properly, and there are no leaks. Most pumps have indicator lights to signal normal operation.
Q: Can the patient lie directly on the air mattress? A: A single cotton bed sheet can be placed over the air mattress for comfort and hygiene, but avoid thick mattress pads or multiple layers as they reduce the pressure-relief effectiveness.
Q: What happens during a power outage? A: The mattress will slowly deflate. Have a standard foam mattress available as backup. Some pumps have battery backup — check your model's specifications.

Features a microprocessor-controlled pump that precisely regulates alternating inflation cycles for optimal therapeutic effectiveness. Premium-grade materials provide durability and patient comfort during extended use. The deep-cell design provides greater pressure relief than standard air mattresses, making it suitable for patients at moderate to high risk of pressure injury. Quiet pump operation ensures patient sleep is not disturbed. The mattress is waterproof, easy to clean, and compatible with standard hospital and home care bed frames.
how_to_use: Place the air mattress on top of the existing bed surface with air cells running horizontally. Connect the pump unit via the tubing connector. name: Air Mattress Tabular
description: Dr. Seibert Tubular Air Mattress — advanced tubular-cell design air mattress providing even, consistent weight distribution for patients at high risk of pressure ulcers. Unlike bubble-cell mattresses, the individual tubular cells run the full width of the bed, creating continuous support lines that distribute body weight more uniformly across the contact surface. This design is especially effective for patients with existing pressure injuries, spinal cord injuries, or those requiring extended bed rest. Electric pump alternates inflation between tube sets on a therapeutic cycle, ensuring no single body area bears sustained pressure. Durable PVC tube construction resists puncture and is waterproof for easy cleaning. Dr. Seibert quality engineering ensures reliable, consistent performance.
how_to_use: Lay the mattress flat on the bed with the tubular cells running horizontally (perpendicular to the patient's body). Connect the electric pump to the mattress via the air tubing. Plug the pump into a power outlet and turn on. Set the pressure level appropriate for the patient's body weight using the adjustment control. The pump will alternate inflation between the two sets of tubes on a timed cycle. Ensure the patient is centred on the mattress with pressure points (sacrum, heels, shoulders) properly supported. Cover with a breathable sheet. Check tube inflation daily — replace the mattress if any tubes fail to inflate. Clean with a damp cloth and disinfectant.

faqs:
Q: What is the difference between tubular and bubble air mattresses? A: Tubular mattresses have long horizontal air cells that alternate in pairs, providing more even pressure distribution across the body. Bubble mattresses have individual round cells. Tubular designs are generally preferred for higher-risk patients.
Q: How do I clean the air mattress? A: Wipe the surface with a damp cloth and mild disinfectant. Do not submerge or machine wash. Ensure the mattress is completely dry before reuse. Inspect for punctures regularly.
Q: Can this mattress be used on a regular bed frame? A: Yes, place the tubular air mattress on top of a standard hospital or home bed. Ensure it lies flat without folding at the edges.

name: Aircurve 10 Vauto Apac Tri 4g
description: ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto APAC with TriPack and 4G Connectivity — advanced auto-adjusting bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP) device with built-in heated humidifier, integrated 4G cellular module, and a complete mask bundle. The VAuto algorithm automatically adjusts both inspiratory (IPAP) and expiratory (EPAP) pressures breath-by-breath, responding in real time to airway obstructions, apnoeas, and flow limitations. Built-in heated humidifier with ClimateLineAir tube delivers optimal temperature and humidity to prevent dryness and nasal congestion. 4G wireless connectivity transmits therapy data directly to the healthcare provider's AirView platform for remote compliance monitoring and therapy adjustments without clinic visits. Intuitive colour LCD displays nightly therapy data and device status.
how_to_use: Set up the device on a stable bedside table within reach of a power outlet. Fill the humidifier water chamber with distilled water up to the maximum line. Connect the ClimateLineAir heated tube to the device and the included mask. Power on the device using the start button. Wear the mask and breathe normally — the VAuto algorithm will auto-adjust pressures throughout the night based on your breathing patterns. In the morning, review your therapy summary on the colour display. Therapy data is automatically transmitted via 4G to your sleep specialist. Empty and rinse the humidifier chamber daily. Replace the water daily with fresh distilled water. Clean the mask cushion, tubing, and chamber weekly.
key_features: VAuto algorithm auto-adjusts IPAP and EPAP pressures breath-by-breath | Built-in heated humidifier with ClimateLineAir tube for optimal comfort | 4G cellular connectivity for remote therapy monitoring via AirView | Colour LCD display shows nightly therapy data and device status | Expiratory pressure relief (EPR) for comfortable exhalation | SmartStart auto on/off when you breathe into the mask | Whisper-quiet Easy-Breathe motor | Complete TriPack bundle includes mask | SD card data recording for detailed therapy analysis
ideal_for: Complex sleep apnoea requiring auto-adjusting bilevel therapy | Central sleep apnoea events during PAP therapy | Obstructive sleep apnoea patients intolerant of fixed CPAP | COPD-obstructive sleep apnoea overlap syndrome | Chronic respiratory failure with sleep-disordered breathing | Patients under remote telehealth monitoring | Sleep apnoea patients requiring humidification for comfort | Healthcare systems needing wireless compliance tracking
faqs:
Q: What is the difference between APAP and CPAP? A: CPAP delivers a single fixed pressure throughout the night. APAP (Auto-PAP) automatically adjusts pressure breath-by-breath based on detected events, providing the minimum effective pressure at any given moment — often more comfortable for users.
Q: Does this device include a humidifier? A: Check the specific bundle or variant. Many ResMed AirCurve 10 models are available with an integrated HumidAir humidifier or can have one added separately.
Q: How do I access my therapy data? A: The AirCurve 10 records therapy data on an SD card. You can also use the myAir app (where available) to track your sleep scores, usage hours, and mask leak data.
Q: How often should I replace filters? A: Replace the standard air filter every month and the hypoallergenic filter every 6 months, or sooner if visibly dirty.

name: Airfit N20 Nasal Mask
description: ResMed AirFit N20 Nasal Mask — premium nasal CPAP/BiPAP mask featuring ResMed's InfinitySeal silicone cushion technology that adapts to a wide range of facial structures for a personalised, leak-free seal without over-tightening. Lightweight frame design sits low on the face, preserving a wide field of vision for reading and watching television before sleep. Magnetic headgear clips snap the mask on and off in the dark with one hand — no buckles or clips to fumble with during nighttime bathroom trips. Quiet, diffused-vent technology disperses exhaled air gently to avoid disturbing a bed partner. The flexible frame moves with the patient during sleep, maintaining seal integrity through position changes.
how_to_use: Select the correct cushion size by measuring the distance from the bridge of the nose to the base of the nose and referring to the ResMed sizing guide. Attach the cushion to the frame by pressing it into place. Connect the headgear clips to each side of the frame. Place the mask over the nose, ensuring the cushion sits comfortably on the nasal bridge and above the upper lip. Pull the headgear over the head and adjust the top and side straps for a secure but comfortable fit — do not over-tighten. Attach the elbow connector and tubing to the front of the mask. Connect the other end of the tubing to your CPAP/BiPAP device. Replace the cushion every 1–3 months, frame every 3–6 months, and headgear every 6 months.

Q: How do I know if this mask size fits me? A: ResMed provides a sizing template that you can print and hold against your face. The cushion should cover your nose comfortably without pressing on the bridge or extending below the nostrils.
Q: How often should I replace the cushion? A: Replace the nasal cushion every 2–4 weeks. Over time, the silicone loses elasticity and the seal degrades, leading to air leaks that reduce therapy effectiveness.
Q: Can I use this mask if I breathe through my mouth? A: The AirFit N20 covers only the nose. If you tend to mouth-breathe during sleep, consider adding a chin strap or switching to a full-face mask for effective therapy.

name: Airfit N30i Mask
description: ResMed AirFit N30i Nasal Cradle Mask — minimalist nasal CPAP/BiPAP mask with a top-of-head tube connection that routes the air hose over the top of the head, giving the patient complete freedom of movement during sleep. The nasal cradle cushion sits gently under the nose with minimal facial contact — no bulky frame over the nose bridge or cheeks. This open-face design reduces feelings of claustrophobia and allows patients to read, watch TV, and wear glasses comfortably while the mask is on. The soft, flexible cradle self-adjusts to maintain a seal across a wide range of sleeping positions. Starter kit includes multiple cushion sizes for personalised fitting.
how_to_use: Select the correct cushion size from the included starter pack options. Attach the nasal cradle cushion to the frame. Place the soft cradle under the nose so it rests gently against the nostrils. Route the tube connector over the top of the head via the headgear channel. Adjust the headgear straps for a light, comfortable hold — the cradle should seal with minimal tightening. Connect the tube to your CPAP/BiPAP device. The top-of-head tube design allows free movement, stomach sleeping, and side-to-side turning without tugging on the mask. Clean the cradle cushion daily with mild soap and warm water. Replace cushion monthly and frame/headgear per manufacturer schedule.

faqs:
Q: What makes the N30i different from other nasal masks? A: The N30i features a top-of-head tube connection and a minimal nasal cradle design, keeping the tubing out of your line of sight and reducing facial contact — ideal for active sleepers and claustrophobia-prone users.
Q: Can I wear glasses or read in bed with this mask? A: Yes, the N30i's top-of-head tube design and minimal nasal cradle leave the face largely unobstructed, allowing you to read, watch TV, or wear glasses comfortably before sleep.
Q: How do I clean the nasal cradle cushion? A: Wash the cushion daily with warm water and mild soap. Rinse thoroughly and air dry. Replace every 2–4 weeks.

name: Airmini Autoset W Apac
description: ResMed AirMini AutoSet — the world's smallest and lightest travel CPAP device, delivering full AutoSet auto-adjusting therapy in an ultra-compact form factor that fits in a carry-on bag, backpack, or overnight bag. Despite its miniature size, the AirMini provides the same clinically proven AutoSet algorithm as the full-sized AirSense 10, automatically detecting and responding to apnoea, hypopnoea, and flow limitation events throughout the night. The innovative HumidX waterless humidification system adds moisture to the air without water chambers, tubes, or risk of spills during travel. Controlled via the AirMini smartphone app for therapy settings, sleep data review, and device management. USB-compatible power — can be used with a portable battery for camping or flights.
how_to_use: Place the AirMini on a stable surface near the bed. Insert the HumidX waterless humidifier cartridge into the mask connector (if using). Connect the compatible ResMed mask to the AirMini using the proprietary short tubing. Download the AirMini app on your smartphone and pair via Bluetooth. Power on the device using the button or via the app. Wear the mask and breathe normally — the AutoSet algorithm adjusts pressure automatically. Review your sleep data each morning in the app. The HumidX cartridge lasts approximately 30 days. Clean the mask and tubing per standard mask cleaning procedures. For travel, disconnect and pack — no water to empty.

Q: Does the AirMini work with all ResMed masks? A: The AirMini is compatible with select ResMed masks including AirFit N20, AirFit P10, AirFit F20, and AirFit F30. Each requires a specific connector.

name: Airsense 10 Autoset Apac
description: ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet APAC — premium auto-adjusting CPAP device with built-in heated humidifier and clinically proven AutoSet algorithm that detects and responds to obstructive apnoea, hypopnoea, and flow limitation events breath-by-breath. The device automatically increases pressure when it detects airway obstruction and lowers it when the airway is clear, ensuring the minimum effective pressure throughout the night for maximum comfort. description: Foley Catheter — indwelling urinary catheter with inflatable retention balloon for continuous urine drainage in patients unable to void independently. The catheter is inserted through the urethra into the bladder, and the balloon is inflated with sterile water to hold the catheter in position, allowing continuous gravity-fed urine drainage into a collection bag. Smooth drainage eyes (openings) at the tip prevent blockage. Two-way design with separate lumens for drainage and balloon inflation. Sterile, individually packaged for single patient use.
how_to_use: For trained medical professionals only. Strict aseptic technique is mandatory. Open the sterile catheter kit. Drape the perineal area. Clean the urethral meatus with antiseptic solution. Lubricate the catheter tip with sterile anaesthetic gel. For males: hold the penis upright and insert the catheter gently until urine begins to flow, then advance 2–3 cm further. For females: separate the labia and insert into the urethral meatus until urine flows, then advance 2–3 cm. Inflate the retention balloon with the specified volume of sterile water (typically 10ml). Gently pull back until the balloon seats at the bladder neck. Connect to a sterile closed drainage bag. Secure the catheter to the patient's thigh. Monitor urine output and colour.

description: HMS Indostim DT Electrical Muscle Stimulator (Rental) — therapeutic electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) device by HMS Medical Systems, available for rental for patients undergoing physiotherapy and rehabilitation. Delivers controlled electrical impulses through electrode pads placed on the skin over target muscle groups to cause involuntary muscle contractions. This stimulation helps maintain muscle mass during immobilisation, re-educates muscles after injury or surgery, reduces pain through gate-control and endorphin release mechanisms, and improves blood circulation to the treated area. Multiple stimulation modes and adjustable intensity settings allow the physiotherapist to customise the treatment programme. Rental option provides access to professional-grade muscle stimulation during the rehabilitation period.
how_to_use: Clean and dry the skin over the target muscle group. Place the self-adhesive electrode pads on the skin as directed by your physiotherapist — typically one pad at each end of the target muscle. Gradually increase the intensity from zero until comfortable muscle contractions are felt — the sensation should be tingling progressing to rhythmic muscle twitching. name: Pulse Oximeter
description: Helyxon pulse oximeter — fingertip device measuring blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) and pulse rate. Non-invasive, instant reading for patient monitoring.
how_to_use: Turn on the device. Place finger (preferably index or middle) into the clip with the nail facing up. Wait 5-10 seconds for a stable reading. Read SpO2 percentage and pulse rate on display. Remove finger to turn off.

faqs:
Q: How accurate is a fingertip pulse oximeter? A: Fingertip pulse oximeters are accurate to ±2% for SpO2 readings between 70–100% under normal conditions. Accuracy may be affected by cold fingers, nail polish, poor circulation, or motion.
Q: What is a normal SpO2 reading? A: Normal SpO2 is 95–100%. Below 90% is considered low and requires medical attention. For COPD patients, your physician may set a different target range.
Q: How do I use it? A: Insert your finger (usually the index finger) fully into the clip. Wait 10–15 seconds for a stable reading. Remove nail polish and ensure your hand is warm for accurate results.

Q: Can I use it for continuous monitoring? A: Fingertip oximeters are designed for spot-check readings, not continuous monitoring. For continuous SpO2 monitoring, use a bedside patient monitor with a dedicated SpO2 probe.

Four-way stretchable fabric conforms to the knee’s natural contours for a secure, non-slip fit during movement. Breathable, moisture-wicking knit reduces heat build-up and perspiration. The elastic compression improves proprioception (joint position sense), reduces minor swelling, and provides stabilising support for mild knee conditions. Open patella design (or closed, model-dependent) allows natural kneecap tracking. Large size.
how_to_use: Pull the sleeve over the foot and slide it up to the knee. Centre the opening (if present) over the kneecap. Smooth out wrinkles for uniform compression. The sleeve should feel snug but not tight enough to cause numbness below the knee. Wear during physical activity, walking, or standing for support. Remove during rest if desired. Sizing: measure knee circumference at the centre of the kneecap. Hand wash with mild detergent; air dry flat. Do not iron or bleach.

name: Elbow Brace (L)
description: Tynor Elbow Brace (Large) — targeted pressure elbow brace with a focussed compression pad positioned over the forearm extensor or flexor muscle origin just below the elbow joint. The brace interrupts the pain-generating muscle pull on the epicondyle (bony elbow point) by applying counter-pressure upstream. Adjustable wraparound strap allows precise tensioning for therapeutic compression without cutting off circulation. Breathable neoprene-blend fabric provides warmth to the affected tendons for pain relief. Large size for standard to larger arm circumference.
how_to_use: Slide the arm through the brace loop with the compression pad facing inward. Position the pad approximately 2–3 cm below the bony prominence of the outer elbow (lateral epicondyle) for tennis elbow, or inner elbow (medial epicondyle) for golfer’s elbow. Tighten the wraparound strap until you feel firm pressure on the muscle belly — enough to reduce pain during gripping/lifting but not so tight that the hand tingles. Wear during provocative activities (typing, gripping, lifting, sports). Remove during rest. Combine with a stretching programme for best results.

name: Elbow Crutch Adjustable
description: Tynor Elbow Crutch (Adjustable) — forearm (Lofstrand) crutch with an ergonomic elbow cuff and height-adjustable aluminium shaft. The forearm cuff wraps around the upper forearm, allowing the user to release the handgrip (for opening doors, holding objects) without the crutch falling away. Provides greater balance control and a more natural gait than underarm crutches. Ergonomic anatomical handgrip reduces hand fatigue during prolonged use. Push-button height adjustment. Non-slip rubber tip for secure traction on all surfaces.
how_to_use: Adjust the shaft height so the handgrip sits at wrist level when standing upright with arms relaxed — the elbow should bend at approximately 15–30 degrees. Insert the forearm through the cuff (cuff should sit 3–5 cm below the elbow). Grip the handle. Walk by advancing the crutch and the affected leg together, then the unaffected leg. The forearm cuff allows you to release the handle to open doors or carry items without dropping the crutch. Inspect rubber tip for wear and replace when smooth.

Replace when the silicone becomes thin, discoloured, or loses its bounce.

name: Hernia Belt (L)
description: Tynor Hernia Belt (Large) — inguinal hernia truss belt with a focussed pressure pad that applies directed compression over the hernia defect site to prevent visceral protrusion (bulging). The adjustable waist strap wraps around the pelvis, and the perineal strap secures between the legs to hold the pad firmly in position over the inguinal canal even during walking, bending, and physical activity. Contoured pressure pad conforms to the groin anatomy for comfortable, effective containment. Large size. Often used as a conservative management option while awaiting hernia surgery or for patients who are not surgical candidates.
how_to_use: Lie flat on your back to allow the hernia to reduce (go back in). Position the pressure pad directly over the hernia site on the inguinal canal. Wrap the waist strap around the pelvis. Thread the perineal strap between the legs and attach to the back of the waist strap. Adjust all straps so the pad applies firm, constant pressure — the hernia should stay reduced (not bulge out) when you stand. Wear during all waking hours and physical activity. Remove for bathing. Readjust if the pad shifts. Consult a surgeon for definitive hernia repair.

Q: What is a hernia belt? A: A hernia belt applies localised pressure over an inguinal or umbilical hernia, keeping the hernia reduced (pushed back in) to relieve discomfort. It is a non-surgical management option or pre/post-surgical support.

name: High Flow Mask
description: High Flow Oxygen Mask with Reservoir Bag — non-rebreather mask for delivering high-concentration oxygen (up to 90–100% FiO₂) to patients with severe respiratory distress. The one-litre reservoir bag stores 100% oxygen between breaths, while one-way flutter valves on the mask body prevent exhaled air from re-entering the bag, ensuring near-pure oxygen delivery with each inhalation. Adjustable metal nose clip and elastic headband provide a secure, comfortable fit. Clear mask body allows visual assessment of the patient’s face. Standard tubing connector for oxygen sources.
how_to_use: Connect the mask tubing to the oxygen source (concentrator, cylinder, or wall supply). Set the flow rate to 10–15 LPM (high flow is essential for this mask type). Allow the reservoir bag to inflate fully before placing the mask on the patient. Place the mask over the patient’s nose and mouth. Adjust the metal nose clip for a snug fit. Stretch the elastic band over the head. Verify that the reservoir bag inflates and deflates slightly with each breath — if the bag collapses completely, increase the flow rate. Monitor SpO₂ continuously.

Q: What is a high-flow oxygen mask? A: A high-flow mask (non-rebreather or Venturi mask) delivers higher oxygen concentrations (60–100%) than a simple mask. It is used for patients requiring high-flow oxygen therapy in acute respiratory distress.
Q: Is this the same as a regular oxygen mask? A: No, high-flow masks have a reservoir bag and one-way valves that prevent room air mixing, delivering higher oxygen concentrations than standard masks.

name: Humidifier Bottle
description: Bubble Humidifier Bottle for Oxygen Therapy — medical-grade humidifier bottle that moistens supplemental oxygen before delivery to the patient, preventing nasal and airway dryness, irritation, and discomfort. Oxygen passes through a tube submerged in sterile water, creating bubbles that pick up moisture. The humidified oxygen then flows through the delivery tubing to the patient’s nasal cannula or mask. Clear graduated bottle allows easy water level monitoring. Standard threaded connector fits most oxygen flow meters and concentrators.
how_to_use: Fill the bottle with sterile or distilled water to the indicated maximum fill line (do NOT use tap water). Screw the lid/connector assembly onto the bottle firmly. Attach the bottle’s inlet connector to the oxygen flow meter or concentrator outlet. Connect the oxygen delivery tubing (to nasal cannula or mask) to the bottle’s outlet port. Turn on the oxygen flow and verify visible bubbling in the water. Change the water DAILY (every 24 hours) to prevent bacterial growth. Refill when the water level drops below the minimum line. Clean or replace the bottle per facility protocol.

Q: How do I prevent algae growth? A: Use distilled water. Clean the bottle daily with warm soapy water. Replace every 3–6 months or when discolouration appears.

The viscoelastic silicone gel deforms under body weight to absorb impact at heel strike and forefoot push-off, reducing stress on the plantar fascia, metatarsal heads, and joints. Anti-slip textured underside grips the shoe interior. Trimmable along marked guidelines for custom fit. Washable and reusable. Large size.
how_to_use: Remove the existing insole from your shoe (if removable). Place the Tynor silicone insole into the shoe with the textured side facing down. If needed, trim along the marked guidelines at the toe end using scissors for a precise fit. Walk normally — the gel cushions each step from heel strike to toe-off. Use in well-fitting enclosed shoes. Clean with mild soap and water; air dry. Replace when the silicone becomes thin, loses cushioning, or shows visible wear.

name: Knee Cap Open Patella (L)
description: Tynor Knee Cap Open Patella (Large) — elastic knee support sleeve with a reinforced opening over the kneecap (patella) that reduces patellar pressure while delivering circumferential compression around the knee joint. The open patella design prevents uncomfortable compression on a sensitive or painful kneecap, and the buttress ring around the opening helps guide the patella through its natural tracking groove during flexion and extension. Four-way stretchable fabric conforms to the knee’s contours for a non-slip, anatomical fit. Breathable, moisture-wicking construction for all-day comfort. Large size.
how_to_use: Pull the sleeve over the foot and slide up to the knee. Centre the patella opening directly over the kneecap — the kneecap should sit within the opening without any fabric pressing on it. Smooth out wrinkles for uniform compression. The sleeve should be snug but not restrict circulation below the knee. Sizing: measure circumference at the centre of the kneecap. Wear during physical activity, walking, or prolonged standing. Remove during rest if desired. Hand wash with mild detergent; air dry.

Q: What is an open patella knee cap? A: An open patella knee cap is a compressive knee sleeve with a hole (opening) over the kneecap. This design reduces patellar pressure, improves tracking, and provides compression around the knee joint.
Q: How is it different from a closed patella knee cap? A: The open design reduces pressure on the kneecap itself, which is beneficial for patellofemoral syndrome, patellar tracking issues, and anterior knee pain.

name: Kinesiology Tape
description: Kinesiology Tape — elastic therapeutic sports tape that mimics the thickness and elasticity of human skin, enabling it to lift the skin microscopically to improve blood and lymphatic circulation in the taped area. The 100% cotton fabric with medical-grade acrylic adhesive is waterproof, breathable, and hypoallergenic, staying in place for 3–5 days through showering, swimming, and sweating. Applied in specific patterns along muscles and joints, it provides support without restricting range of motion — unlike rigid athletic tape. Latex-free adhesive activates with body heat for secure, comfortable wear.
how_to_use: Cut the tape to the desired length. Round the corners with scissors (this prevents peeling). For the anchor end: apply 2–3 cm with zero stretch directly to the skin. For the middle portion: stretch the tape to 25–75% (depending on the technique) and apply along the target muscle or around the joint. For the tail end: apply the last 2–3 cm with zero stretch. Rub briskly over the applied tape for 10–15 seconds to activate the heat-sensitive adhesive. Tape may be worn for 3–5 days. To remove: peel slowly in the direction of hair growth while pressing down on the skin ahead of the peel. Apply to clean, dry, oil-free skin.

ideal_for: Sports injury recovery and prevention | Muscle strain support (hamstring, calf, shoulder) | Joint support (ankle, knee, wrist) | Lymphatic drainage and swelling reduction | Postural correction | Physiotherapy and rehabilitation | Exercise performance support | Bruise and oedema management
faqs:
Q: What is kinesiology tape? A: Kinesiology tape is an elastic therapeutic tape applied to the skin to support muscles and joints, reduce pain and inflammation, and improve circulation — without restricting range of motion.
Q: How long can I leave it on? A: Kinesiology tape can remain on the skin for 3–5 days, even through showering and sweating. It is water-resistant and breathable.
Q: Do I need training to apply it? A: For best results, have a physiotherapist demonstrate the correct taping technique for your specific condition. Incorrect application reduces effectiveness.

name: Knee Brace Long Type (L)
description: Tynor Knee Brace Long Type (Large) — extended-length hinged knee brace providing comprehensive above-and-below-joint stabilisation with bilateral metal hinges. The long wraparound design covers from mid-thigh to mid-calf, delivering circumferential support and compression across the entire knee complex. Bilateral polycentric hinges replicate the knee’s natural arc of motion, allowing controlled flexion and extension while preventing harmful lateral (valgus/varus) and rotational forces. Multiple adjustable velcro straps enable customised fit and compression. Breathable fabric with padded interior for extended-wear comfort. Large size.
how_to_use: Open the brace fully. Position behind the knee with the bilateral hinges aligned to the joint line (the hinge pivot point should be level with the centre of the kneecap). Wrap the brace around the leg. Secure all velcro straps from bottom to top: first the lower leg straps, then the upper thigh straps. Adjust each strap for firm, even compression without restricting circulation. The hinges should allow smooth bending without clicking or catching. Wear during activity as directed. For post-surgical use, follow your surgeon’s instructions on range-of-motion restrictions.

Apply the abdominal front panel and secure all closure straps, adjusting tension for firm immobilization without respiratory restriction. Verify the patient can breathe comfortably. Check skin at all contact points daily. Wear as prescribed, typically during all upright activities. Remove for skin inspection and hygiene as directed.
